title: Intel Q3 2026 Earnings Data Center Soars While PC Faces Memory Pressure
gist: Intel's Q3 2026 revenue rose 21% year over year to $16.5B. Data Center and AI revenue jumped 78% to $7.3B, while client PC revenue fell 5% to $8.1B as DRAM and NAND shortages pushed system costs up. STH argues that memory being priced for its value in AI nodes is draining the consumer PC market while AI and data center markets boom, and that substrate shortages limit Xeon supply.

insights.claim: Intel's Q3 2026 revenue was $16.5 billion, up 21% year over year, with 44.1% non-GAAP gross margin and $0.52 non-GAAP EPS. STH notes the growth comes off a weak year-ago quarter.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Intel's headline recovery partly reflects an easy comparison with a weak Q3 2025.
insights.quote: Intel reported third-quarter 2026 earnings with revenue of $16.5 billion, up 21% year-over-year.

themes.theme: Data center surge and supply limits

insights.claim: Intel's Data Center and AI group had Q3 2026 revenue of $7.3 billion, up 78% year over year, with $3.0 billion operating income at a 41.5% margin. CFO David Zinsner called it Intel's strongest data center revenue growth in 15 years.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Data center has become Intel's profit engine, with segment margins above 40%.
insights.quote: David Zinsner, Intel’s CFO, called it Intel’s strongest data center revenue growth in 15 years.

insights.claim: Server CPU demand has shifted toward AMD's 192-core Turin parts, which Intel has no direct competitor for. Partners say Intel's Xeon 6 still sells because supply is so tight that basically everything is selling.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Intel's data center strength reflects an industry-wide shortage more than competitive wins, and its share could be exposed if supply normalizes.
insights.quote: partners tell us that Xeon 6 is selling because basically everything is selling

insights.claim: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan said Intel's immediate priority is unlocking more supply to meet extraordinary Xeon demand, but substrate availability is limiting output and will take time to ease. Intel appears to be steering 18A supply toward the data center, depending on substrate availability.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Packaging substrates, not wafers, are the bottleneck for Intel's server revenue in the near term.
insights.quote: he said that substrate availability is limiting output and it would take some time to ease
insights.locator: Demand is strong across hyperscale, enterprise,

insights.claim: Intel's Xeon 6 sales and pricing are being lifted by the NVIDIA-Intel investment and by the many NVIDIA GPU systems that use Intel Xeon host CPUs.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Intel's server CPU business is riding on NVIDIA's AI system build-outs.
insights.quote: the NVIDIA-Intel investment and the many NVIDIA GPU-based systems with Intel Xeon CPUs are helping drive Xeon 6 sales and push pricing up
insights.locator: We do not cover all earnings

insights.claim: Intel's Client Computing and Physical AI Group revenue fell 5% year over year to $8.1 billion. Intel blamed industry-wide memory shortages, with higher DRAM and NAND prices pushing system costs up and hurting PC demand.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Memory inflation is shrinking the PC market Intel can address.
insights.quote: Higher DRAM and NAND prices are pushing system costs up and hurting demand.
insights.locator: The client side looks very different.

insights.claim: Intel expects the PC slowdown to last at least through the first half of 2027, with memory and NAND pricing pressure continuing into 2027. STH saw nothing in the call suggesting memory prices would fall in Q1.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Expect client PC system costs to stay high and PC volumes to stay weak through 1H 2027, while memory makers keep pricing power.
insights.quote: Memory and NAND pricing pressure is expected to persist into 2027, which means client system costs are likely to stay elevated for a while longer.

insights.claim: DRAM and NAND are being priced for the value they add in AI nodes. That is pushing down demand for PCs that don't run AI locally and shrinking the client market, so fewer small companies innovate on PC form factors, while the data center market sees the opposite.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: AI demand is pulling memory supply away from consumer PCs, which hurts mini PC and small form-factor vendors.
insights.quote: Right now, DRAM and NAND are being priced for the value they bring attached to AI nodes.
insights.locator: We do not cover all earnings

insights.claim: Intel Foundry's Q3 2026 revenue was $6.7 billion, up 58% year over year, but that includes intersegment transactions. Its operating loss narrowed to $1.9 billion (-27.7% margin) from $2.3 billion a year earlier, helped by better yields and cycle times that cut wafer costs. Intel shipped the 14A 0.9 PDK in October as committed.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Foundry losses are narrowing, but its revenue growth is mostly internal and doesn't show external customer traction yet.
insights.quote: The segment still recorded an operating loss of $1.9 billion with a negative 27.7% margin, but that is narrower than the $2.3 billion loss a year ago.
